messages:
alex: heads-up — customer reports agent in their prod cluster never reaches control plane. getting repeated TLS timeouts and DNS NXDOMAIN for controlplane.redwood.internal. customer applied a CNI/global deny-everything policy this morning.
megan: can you paste the agent logs + the coredns dig output? likely egress/DNS blocked. any special svcaccount/netpol that would stop kube-dns?
alex: logs (redacted):
```
2024-11-08T12:03:21Z ERROR agent: tls handshake timeout connecting to https://controlplane.redwood.internal:443
2024-11-08T12:03:21Z WARN  resolver: lookup controlplane.redwood.internal: no such host
```
kubectl exec -n kube-system coredns -- dig +short controlplane.redwood.internal @10.96.0.10
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short controlplane.redwood.internal @10.96.0.10
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
ivan: that dig timeout is the smoking gun. if their NetworkPolicy denies UDP/TCP 53 or prevents kube-dns from egressing to upstream resolvers, pod DNS lookups will fail and agent can't resolve controlplane. also if they only allow DNS to a specific set but not those upstream IPs, you'll see NXDOMAIN/timeouts.
megan: ask customer to run these quick checks and paste outputs: 1) `kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide` 2) `kubectl run -n redwood --rm -i --tty dns-test --image=busybox --restart=Never -- sh` then inside: `nslookup controlplane.redwood.internal` and `wget -S https://controlplane.redwood.internal`
alex: they ran busybox test and nslookup fails with "can't reach nameserver". they also sent a Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
spec:
  selector: all()
  types:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - action: Deny
```
ivan: yep — explicit deny-everything will block egress unless they add allows. action items: 1) ask customer to add permissive egress to allow DNS and control-plane IPs OR add exceptions for the redwood agent namespace/serviceAccount. 2) if they use an allowlist model, provide exact ports/IPs we need.
megan: here's suggested NetworkPolicy they can apply in the `redwood` namespace (works with CNI allowlist style; replace `CONTROL_PLANE_IP` with IP(s) from our infra team):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: CONTROL_PLANE_IP/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.10/32  # cluster DNS (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```
alex: also ask them to allow egress to their upstream resolver(s) (e.g., 8.8.8.8 or their on-prem DNS) on UDP/TCP 53 if kube-dns forwards.
ivan: FYI if they're running egress NAT at node level, ensure node firewall allows outbound 443 to CONTROL_PLANE_IPs; NetworkPolicy won't affect node-to-internet rules.
megan: small repro snippet to give to eng if needed:
```
# inside cluster, blocked path
$ kubectl run -i --tty debug --image=busybox --restart=Never --rm -- nslookup controlplane.redwood.internal
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
alex: customer applied change and now sees agent register but warned about intermittent DNS latency; we should follow up with ops to share the control-plane CIDR and confirm ports. tagging @oncall-bot to track SLA window. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-271 — "ACME: agent reg fail due to egress/DNS block" assigned to network-eng.
megan: I'll draft the outbound CIDR/ports list and send to customer with the NetworkPolicy/YAML. we should also add a short KB about 'Redwood agent requirements for private clusters' in support docs.
ivan: sounds good. closing for now unless they report TLS errors after DNS fixed. :white_check_mark:
